summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host and install metadata to hardcoded bare IP
details: The package is a dependency-confusion probe targeting the internal `@ecg-internal` scope. `package.json` declares a `postinstall` of `node beacon.cjs`, and `index.js` (the declared `main`) also calls `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at load time, so the beacon fires both on `npm install` and on `require`. `beacon.cjs` POSTs a JSON body containing the package name, `os.hostname()`, the install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc` over plain HTTP. `index.js` exports a `Proxy` whose `get` trap returns a no-op function for any property access, so a consuming build that imports the real internal module's API does not crash while the beacon runs. The package description ("Compatibility shim.") and the beacon's cover-string framing are inconsistent with the actual behavior; the package has no functional code beyond the exfiltration callback.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
